title: Details
subtitle: A summary line that opens to show more, such as the answer to a question.

tutorial.p: Details shows a short summary and hides the content under it until the reader clicks the summary. Use it for questions and answers, or for detail most readers can skip. A reader who never opens it never sees the content, so keep what every reader needs out of it.
No template, template part or theme pattern on this site uses Details, so it appears only where an editor adds it.

steps.text: Open the + (block inserter) at the top left, type details in the search field and click Details.
steps.alt: The block inserter searched for details, with the Details tile outlined in red

steps.text: Or type /details in an empty paragraph and choose Details from the list.
steps.alt: An empty paragraph reading /details, with Details offered in the list below it

steps.text: The block appears with Write summary… beside a triangle. Click it and type the summary.
steps.alt: A Details block just added, reading Write summary… beside a triangle, with its toolbar above

steps.text: Click Type / to add a hidden block under the summary and type the content. Pressing Enter in the summary does not move there.
steps.alt: A Details block with the summary Who can test this site? and the content Anyone with an account on it. below it

steps.text: Save the page (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).

tutorial.alt: The sidebar for Details, with the Open by default switch off under Settings

tutorial.p: A Details block starts closed on the site. To show its content when the page loads, turn on Open by default under Settings in the sidebar. The reader can still close it by clicking the summary.
Any block can go in the content, such as a paragraph, a list or an image, and more than one. The summary holds text, with Bold and Italic in its toolbar.

examples.p: As every Details block starts. Click the summary to open it.

examples.block:
Who can test this site?

Anyone with an account on it. Testers sign in, open a page to test and work through its checklist.

What does a Fail need?

A comment saying what went wrong. A Fail cannot be saved without one.

What to include in a report
  • The page URL
  • A screenshot
  • What you did, what you expected and what happened

What happens to the results of a step after the checklist has been rewritten and the step has been reworded or deleted?

Rewording a step keeps its results. Deleting it leaves its results in the Results list.

checklist_intro.p: Tickets: none. This is a demonstration checklist for core's Details block on Twenty Twenty-Five.

steps.step: Add the block and save it
steps.alt: A Details block with the summary Who can test this site? and the content Anyone with an account on it. below it
instructions: Create a new page and close Choose a pattern.
Type a summary, then click Type / to add a hidden block and type the content.
Save the draft (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).
Reload the page (Mac: Command + R, Windows: Ctrl + R).
steps.expected: After the reload the summary and the content are still there, with no "Block contains unexpected or invalid content." message.

steps.step: Open it by default and add a list
steps.alt: The sidebar for Details, with the Open by default switch off under Settings
instructions: In the same draft, select the Details block and turn on Open by default in the sidebar.
Add a List under the content you typed, with two items.
Save the draft (Mac: Command + S, Windows: Ctrl + S).
Preview the draft (laptop icon at the top right → Preview in new tab).
expected: The list sits inside the block, under the first content.
In the preview the content and the list show without clicking the summary.

checklist.section: Front end at desktop width (a full-width laptop or desktop window)

steps.step: Click the summary of the first example on this page, then click it again.
steps.expected: The content opens under the summary, and the second click closes it.

steps.step: Reload this page and look at the second example.
steps.expected: Its content shows without clicking the summary.

steps.step: Compare the examples on this page with the desktop design.
steps.expected: Colours, fonts, the triangle and spacing match the design.

checklist.section: Front end at mobile width (a phone, or a window about 390px wide)

steps.step: Open each example on this page.
steps.expected: Each opens under its summary, and the page does not scroll sideways.

steps.step: Compare the examples with the mobile design.
steps.expected: Colours, fonts, the triangle and spacing match the design.

steps.step: Look at the example with the long summary.
steps.expected: The summary wraps over several lines beside the triangle, with no text cut off.

steps.step: Press Tab until the summary of the first example is selected, then press Enter twice.
steps.expected: The summary shows a focus outline. The first Enter opens the content, and the second closes it.

steps.step: Zoom the browser to 200% and look at the examples (Mac: Command + +, Windows: Ctrl + +).
steps.expected: Nothing overlaps or is cut off.
